newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania interbank leu lower, retail rates firmer.
newsitem.headline: Romania interbank leu lower, retail rates firmer.

text.p: Romania's leu inched down to 3,495/3,515 to the dollar on an interbank market unmoved by the victory of centrist reformer Emil Constantinescu in Sunday's presidential elections.

But the election of the country's first reformist president of the modern era boosted the leu on retail markets, where it rebounded to 4,600/4,900 on Monday after an all-time low of 5,050/150 over the weekend.
"Everyone is waiting for heaven on Earth after Constantinescu's win. So, the leu gained some 400 units against the greenback on our market," said the manager at a Bucharest exchange house.
The leu has weakened some 44 percent in the past month on the retail market, which has proved more sensitive to political events, forecasts and seasonal trends.

The interbank market remained dull with operators hoping trade would revive when the incoming government delivers its promised reform package. The reform package is expected to include the liberalisation of the market to let the leu head toward a more realistic value, now obtained only in cross deals.
Cross quotes of other currencies offer a leu-dollar price between 4,000 to 4,400.
Short-term rates slipped towards 39-40 percent from 44-45 percent as borrowers failed to show up on a slightly overliquid money market.
